4. **Shift 4 (Thu 26 Mar, NYC)**: 08:00 – 10:00 EDT. Duration = 2 hours. (4.2 OK)

WTS-4 (extract)
4.1 Minimum rest. Between the end of one shift and the start of the next there must be at least 11 hours of rest.
4.2 Maximum shift length. No single shift may exceed 10 hours.
4.3 Weekly maximum. Hours worked in a rota week must not exceed 48. A rota week runs from Monday 00:00 to Sunday 24:00 in the time zone of the employee's home office; a shift is attributed to the rota week in which it starts.

4.5 Breaks. Paid on-queue breaks are part of the shift and are not deducted.
4.6 Standby. Standby (reachable by phone, not logged in) is not a shift and is not counted, but a call-out during standby starts a shift.

Fri 27 Mar  NYC queue   23:00 – Sat 28 Mar 09:00   (quarter-end batch watch)
Sat 28 Mar  —
Sun 29 Mar  BER queue   01:00 – 12:00   (covering Berlin; Berlin L2 on leave)

Zone reference printed on the rota export:

Europe/Berlin — CET (UTC+1) until Sun 29 Mar 2026 02:00 local, when clocks are set forward to 03:00; CEST (UTC+2) from then until Sun 25 Oct 2026.

call.text: {"rationale":"The question asks if Priya Anand's week-13 rota complies with WTS-4 sections 4.1, 4.2, and 4.3. Section 4.3 states that a rota week runs from Monday 00:00 to Sunday 24:00 in the employee's home office time zone (NYC). The rota shows a shift starting on Sunday 29 Mar in the BER queue. According to section 4.4, shift start times are recorded in the local time of the office being covered. Therefore, the Sunday shift starts at 01:00 BER time. Converting 01:00 BER (CET, UTC+1) to NYC time (EST, UTC-5) results in a start time of 18:00 the previous day (Saturday 28 Mar). Since the shift started on Saturday, it falls within the NYC rota week (Mon 23 Mar – Sun 24 Mar EST). The shift duration is 11 hours (01:00 to 12:00), which breaches section 4.2 (max 10h). Additionally, the tool summary lists 49.0 planned hours, which breaches section 4.3 (max 48h). Since at least one criterion is breached, the answer is no.", "p":[1.0,0.0]}
